Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
312 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
All coastal flood hazards have expired.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Showers this afternoon, then breezy and seasonable through
Saturday. 

2) Frontal system will bring another chance of rain to the area
late Sunday night into Monday. Gusty winds on Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

.KEY MESSAGE 1...
An upper low passing to the north and west this evening will be
preceded by a band of showers tracking west to east across the 
area the next few hours. The associated surface lows over 
upstate NY will deepen some while passing to the north tonight 
into Saturday. At the same time, high pressure gradually builds 
in from the south and west through Sunday morning. This will 
maintain a sufficient pressure gradient across the area for 
gusty winds to continue, veering from the SW to W overnight. 
Gusts will be highest near the coast at 20 to 30 mph, strongest 
during the daytime hours. In addition, with deep-layered 
cyclonic flow, expect plenty of clouds but with breaks at times.
Skies will clear from SW to NW late Saturday afternoon into the
evening.

Gusty winds and clouds will limit radiational cooling tonight, 
with lows mainly around 40. Highs Saturday will be in the lower
50s. This is slightly above normal for highs, but about 5-8
degrees above normal for lows. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
High pressure on Sunday gives way to an approaching frontal
system with a slightly warmer day and less wind. Amplifying Pac
jet energy will carve out a deepening upper trough over the
Mississippi Valley on Sunday. There is some interaction with the
northern branch of the polar jet, with even a slight negative
tilt as the upper trough approaches the eastern seaboard Monday
morning. This will result in a rapidly deepening low passing to
our north and a period of moderate rain along and ahead of the
cold front. The system is progressive enough at this time that 
rainfall amounts are forecast at half an inch or less. Much of 
the rain will be over by afternoon. In addition, south winds 
ahead the system will ramp up Sunday night, veering to the W on 
Monday, with potential gusts of 30 to 40 mph. There is a chance
to meet marginal wind advisory criteria. Winds will then 
gradually subside Monday night.

&&

.AVIATION /20Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The terminals will remain between departing low pressure and high 
pressure to the south through Saturday.

Flight categories will fluctuate between VFR and MVFR through the 
TAF period. A brief period of -RA and potentially MVFR is expected 
through early evening. VFR may then prevail tonight at most 
terminals with lingering MVFR well NW of the NYC metros.
MVFR should then prevail after 12-13z Saturday. Any MVFR ceilings 
look to be from 025-030 with low potential for around 020 at KSWF 
and KHPN. 

SSW winds 15-20 kt with gusts around 25 kt through early this 
evening. Peak gusts could reach 30 kt at times, especially at NYC 
and coastal terminals. Winds veer to the SW-W tonight with winds 
weakening a bit, but gusts around 20 kt still possible at NYC 
terminals. Gusts at outlying terminals may drop off late 
tonight/early Saturday. W winds around 15 kt with gusts 20-25 kt 
expected after 13z. 

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Fluctuations between VFR and MVFR possible this afternoon/early 
evening. Brief period of MVFR possible overnight. 

Chance VFR prevails Saturday with any MVFR brief.

Wind gusts could briefly drop off at JFK, LGA, and EWR 06z-13z.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Saturday through Wednesday... 

Saturday Afternoon: MVFR ceilings possible. W winds G20-25kt, 
diminishing in the evening and at night.

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night-Monday: Rain likely with MVFR or lower conditions after 
midnight through early Monday morning. Rain could persist east of 
NYC terminals after sunrise, but improving conditions likely through 
the day. S winds G20-30 kt late Sunday night, then W G 25-35 kt on 
Monday. Winds diminish Monday Night.

Tuesday-Wednesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SW-W Gales will continue on much of the ocean into tonight, 
with the exception of Sandy Hook to Fire Island Inlet out 20 nm.
The latter may see a few gusts hit 35 kt, but generally closer 
to 30 kt. Seas on the ocean at 12 to 16 ft will gradually 
subside through Saturday night. 

With deepening low pressure passing to the north tonight in 
Saturday. SCA conditions are expected across all waters Saturday
and on the ocean into Saturday night before wind and seas 
subside below criteria. High pressure briefly builds across the
waters late Saturday night into Sunday, then offshore ahead of 
strong frontal system that will bring the potential for gales 
late Sunday night into Monday.
